gloss: tip of the tongue; glib talk

definitions.explanation: the front part of the tongue, especially as used in tasting or pronouncing sounds

definitions.gloss: glib talk; smooth talking; lip service
definitions.explanation: insincere or superficial speech, often used negatively to describe someone who is good at talking but not trustworthy

examples.japanese: {舌先|したさき}でソースの{味|あじ}を{確|たし}かめた。
examples.english: I tasted the sauce with the tip of my tongue.

examples.japanese: {辛|から}いものを{食|た}べると{舌先|したさき}がピリピリする。
examples.english: When I eat spicy food, my tongue tip tingles.

examples.japanese: {舌先|したさき}にレモンの{酸味|さんみ}が{広|ひろ}がった。
examples.english: The sourness of lemon spread across the tip of my tongue.

examples.japanese: {舌先|したさき}だけの{約束|やくそく}は{信用|しんよう}できない。
examples.english: Promises that are just lip service can't be trusted.

examples.japanese: あの{営業|えいぎょう}マンは{舌先|したさき}がうまい。
examples.english: That salesman has a smooth tongue.

examples.japanese: {舌先|したさき}{三寸|さんずん}で{人|ひと}を{騙|だま}すような{真似|まね}はするな。
examples.english: Don't do things like deceiving people with glib talk.

notes:
{舌先|したさき} has both a literal meaning (tip of the tongue) and a figurative meaning (glib or insincere talk).

SENSE 1 — LITERAL:
The physical tip of the tongue, as used in tasting or pronunciation.
- {舌先|したさき}で{味|あじ}を{確|たし}かめる: to check the taste with the tip of the tongue

SENSE 2 — FIGURATIVE:
Insincere, superficial speech. Always negative in connotation.
- {舌先|したさき}だけの{約束|やくそく}: a promise that's just lip service
- {舌先|したさき}がうまい: smooth-tongued, glib

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
{舌先|したさき}{三寸|さんずん} (literally "three inches of tongue tip") means using smooth talk to deceive others. Strongly negative.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {口先|くちさき}: lip service, glib talk (very similar to sense 2)
- {口|くち}がうまい: smooth-talking
- {口車|くちぐるま}に{乗|の}る: to be taken in by smooth talk
